newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chernomyrdin denies young and old split in cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Chernomyrdin denies young and old split in cabinet.

text.p: Veteran Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin denied on Sunday there was a split in his government between new young ministers and older politicians over Russia's reform course.

President Boris Yeltsin named dynamic young reformers Anatoly Chubais and Boris Nemtsov to a revamped cabinet in March but left the more conservative Chernomyrdin in charge as the government sought to accelerate its economic changes.

"There is no split," Chernomyrdin told reporters after laying a wreath at Moscow's Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. "All decisions taken by the government are worked out and executed by the entire government and not one person."
Nemtsov is 37 and Chubais 42. Chernomyrdin is 60 next April.

He said a controversial proposal to dismantle generous Soviet-era housing subsidies and other welfare benefits was crucial. Communists and many others fear the scheme would leave impoverished Russians even worse off.
"Without this reform we cannot improve the country's economy," he said. "We want to carry out this reform to make things better, not worse."
Chernomyrdin did not refer to Monday's scheduled debate and vote in the Communist-dominated State Duma lower house of parliament on the government's proposed overall budget cuts.
